NVIDIA Bantah RTX 5090 Discontinue — Tetap Dikirim, Tapi Pasokan Ketat

Meskipun kami melihat banyak laporan yang mengindikasikan penghentian GPU andalan Blackwell GeForce, NVIDIA, di sisi lain, membantah laporan tersebut. Beberapa publikasi Taiwan telah melaporkan bantahan NVIDIA atas laporan bahwa RTX 5090 dihentikan. bertujuan untuk memasok die GB202 untuk seri RTX PRO. Menurut 4gamers, nvidia jeff fisher menanggapi rumor 5090 eol. 4gamers menulis: jeff fisher: Rantai pasokan (kapasitas) memang agak terbatas, tetapi NVIDIA berusaha sekuat tenaga untuk memasarkan produk tersebut. Meskipun ada varian lain dari RTX 5090, varian ini sebenarnya tidak dihentikan dan NVIDIA akan terus mengirimkannya, dan ini sangat penting. oleh gemini: Rantai pasokan (dan… pic.twitter.com/aWToz3PIU1

Laporan menunjukkan bahwa NVIDIA akan mengganti RTX 5090 dengan RTX 5080 24 GB sebagai GPU andalan baru seri RTX 50. Namun, NVIDIA tidak mengomentari laporan tersebut hingga saat ini, ketika wakil presiden senior NVIDIA membantah rumor tersebut. SVP NVIDIA, Jeff Fisher, dilaporkan mengatakan kepada media Taiwan bahwa laporan tentang penghentian RTX 5090 tidak benar dan bahwa GPU tetap menjadi produk inti yang sangat penting. Selain itu, dia mengatakan bahwa RTX 5090 akan terus dikirimkan, membantah laporan EOL. Namun, Jeff juga mengakui adanya kendala pasokan yang parah. Pernyataan tersebut tampaknya menyoroti memburuknya ketersediaan RTX 5090, yang telah mencapai $5000+ di sebagian besar wilayah. Pernyataan Jeff mengenai pasokan RTX 5090 dikutip oleh 4Gamers dan CNA (Kantor Berita Pusat Taiwan). Hal yang sama juga diterbitkan oleh SJTV (TV Satelit Shin Ji). Sesuai laporan, Jeff Fisher datang ke Taiwan untuk menghadiri pesta Peluncuran RTX Spark di Taipei, di mana dia memberikan komentarnya tentang rumor RTX 5090. Jeff kabarnya juga menyoroti pentingnya bisnis Gaming dan GeForce NVIDIA dan mengatakan bahwa tidak akan ada NVIDIA saat ini tanpa segmen ini. Jika apa yang dikatakan Jeff mengenai RTX 5090 benar adanya, maka kita memerlukan jawaban mengapa RTX 5090 tiba-tiba menghilang dari pasaran NVIDIA. Selain itu, pengecer besar seperti Micro Center menghapus GPU dari rak mereka. Apakah NVIDIA tiba-tiba melanjutkan produksi karena reaksi negatif? Ataukah memang terjadi gangguan pada rantai pasok karena kelangkaan? Saya pikir kita akan segera mengetahuinya. Tentang Penulis : Sarfraz Khan adalah reporter perangkat keras dengan fokus pada komponen PC dan komunitas pembuat. Dengan pengalaman bertahun-tahun menulis tentang perangkat keras PC dan laptop, karyanya telah ditampilkan di beberapa publikasi teknologi terkemuka. Pengalaman langsung Sarfraz ditunjukkan melalui pengalaman langsungnya dalam menggunakan dan membandingkan konfigurasi perangkat keras yang berbeda, memberikan wawasan praktis dan relevan bagi pengguna sehari-hari. Analisis teknisnya dihormati oleh rekan-rekan di komunitas antusias dan telah dikutip oleh situs perangkat keras khusus seperti Igor's Lab di Jerman. Ikuti Wccftech di Google untuk mendapatkan lebih banyak liputan berita kami di feed Anda.

Berita ini disusun dari laporan Wccftech.

title: Intel Perkenalkan Xeon 6+ 'Clearwater Forest': CPU 18A Pertama dengan 288 E-Core untuk Telekomunikasi & Edge AI
summary: Each CPU contains up to 288 Efficiency-cores
content:
Intel Perkenalkan Xeon 6+ 'Clearwater Forest': CPU 18A Pertama dengan 288 E-Core untuk Telekomunikasi & Edge AI

Each CPU contains up to 288 Efficiency-cores

Intel has launched its Xeon 6+ CPU, targeting artificial intelligence (AI) networks and data center applications. Unveiled by the company at Mobile World Congress, currently taking place in Barcelona, the processor - codenamed “Clearwater Forest” – is Intel’s most advanced CPU to date. Fabricated using the company’s 18A (1.8nm) process node technology, the Xeon 6+ CPUs contain up to 288 E-cores (Efficiency-cores) that combine 12 chiplets on a single packet, alongside three base tiles made using Intel’s 7nm technology and two I/O tiles made using 10nm technology. The chiplets also contain 24 energy-efficient Darkmont cores per tile. Each Intel Xeon 6+ CPU has 12 memory channels capable of supporting DDR5-8000, in addition to 96 PCIe 5.0 lanes, and 64 CXL 2.0 lanes. Featuring Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), QuickAssist Technology (QAT), and Intel vRAN Boost technologies, in a blog post , Kevork Kechichian, EVP & GM of Intel’s Data Center Group, said the CPUs will unify “RAN, Core, Edge AI, and security on one open platform architecture to turn infrastructure into opportunity on the road to 6G.”

Kechichian went on to outline three customer use cases in his blog, including a partnership between AT&T, Ericsson, and Intel to build a “open, programmable and reliable RAN network” powered by Intel Xeon hardware. Rakuten Mobile and Vodafone have also committed to deploying Intel Xeon 6 processors, he noted. “As customer needs evolve toward platforms that offer predictable performance, strong reliability, and efficient scalability to reduce TCO, Intel is advancing to the next step in the Xeon 6 roadmap: Intel Xeon 6+,” Kechichian wrote. “From 5G infrastructure to cloud‑native applications, these processors are engineered to optimize performance, efficiency, and cost, redefining data center economics on the road to 6G.”

Intel launched its Xeon 6700/6500 series in February 2025 . Describing them as the “ideal CPU for modern data centers” due to their ability to pair “exceptionally well with a GPU as a host node CPU,” the Intel Xeon 6 portfolio delivers an average of 1.4x better performance when compared to 5th Gen Intel Xeon processors across a “wide range of enterprise workloads.”

According to Intel, the Xeon 6+ series is expected to launch in the first half of 2026.

content:
Chip Xiaomi XRING Salip Samsung Exynos di Peringkat AnTuTu Q3 2026

Tambahkan GIZMOCHINA sebagai Sumber Pilihan di Google

AnTuTu telah merilis data Q3 2026 mengenai pangsa prosesor Android di Tiongkok, dan chip XRING Xiaomi secara mengejutkan berada di peringkat ketiga, di atas Exynos dari Samsung. Tidak mengherankan, Qualcomm mendominasi pasar dengan pangsa 68,9%, sementara MediaTek menguasai 28,9%. Berikut perbandingan merek prosesor:

Qualcomm dan MediaTek bersama-sama menyumbang 97,8% penggunaan, sehingga menyisakan sedikit ruang bagi pembuat chip lainnya. Qualcomm memimpin, khususnya dalam ponsel andalan dan ponsel kelas menengah atas, sementara MediaTek bersaing di segmen harga yang lebih luas, termasuk perangkat berbiaya rendah dan kelas menengah. Pangsa Xiaomi sebesar 1,2% memang kecil jika dibandingkan dengan dua perusahaan teratas, namun peringkat ketiga patut dipuji mengingat terbatasnya jumlah ponsel yang menjalankan chipnya. Berbeda dengan Qualcomm dan MediaTek, Xiaomi menggunakan prosesor XRING di perangkatnya sendiri dibandingkan memasoknya ke merek ponsel pintar lain. Posisinya di depan Samsung menunjukkan bahwa XRING mendapatkan daya tarik di antara pengguna Android yang terwakili dalam data AnTuTu. Selain itu, Xiaomi 18 Fold, yang ditenagai oleh XRING O3, menempati posisi teratas dalam peringkat kinerja AnTuTu bulan September, mengungguli Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 dan Dimensity 9600 Pro. Xiaomi meluncurkan Xiaomi 18 Fold pada bulan September sebagai ponsel pertama dengan XRING O3. Perusahaan belum mengumumkan peluncuran internasionalnya, sehingga ponsel dan prosesor terbarunya masih terbatas pada pasar Cina untuk saat ini. Jangan lewatkan apa pun! Bergabunglah dengan komunitas Telegram kami untuk pembaruan instan dan dapatkan buletin harian gratis kami untuk berita teknologi terbaik! Untuk pembaruan harian lainnya, silakan kunjungi Bagian Berita kami.

Berita ini disusun dari laporan GizmoChina.

DeepSeek Rilis V4.1-Flash-1017: Bobot Open-Source MIT + API Search Web, Unggul di DeepSWE

DeepSeek memposting V4.1-Flash-1017 ke Hugging Face pada 17 Oktober 2026 di bawah lisensi MIT, memasangkan penurunan bobot dengan kartu tarif terbuka untuk API Penelusuran dan Pengambilan seharga $0,75 per 1.000 permintaan yang berhasil. Kartu model menggambarkan rilis ini sebagai "pembaruan kecil untuk DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, memberikan peningkatan substansial dalam penalaran, pengkodean, tugas agen, dan tolok ukur visual," dan memuji pembaruan tersebut dengan mengurangi "waktu pelaksanaan tugas dan panjang keluaran, memungkinkan pengguna menyelesaikan tugas lebih cepat dan dengan biaya lebih rendah."

Skor utama adalah 77,0 pada DeepSWE v1.1, naik dari Flash sebelumnya 74,2 dan mengungguli Claude Opus 5 (74,0) dan GPT-5.6 Sol (73,0) pada tolok ukur pengkodean spesifik tersebut, menurut MarkTechPost . Terminal-Bench 4.0 melompat ke 42,3 dari 31,2. MarkTechPost melaporkan pos pemeriksaan baru ini mengalahkan Flash sebelumnya pada 11 tolok ukur DeepSeek yang diterbitkan, sebesar 2,0 hingga 11,1 poin. Secara logika, Opus 5 masih memimpin: HLE berada pada 42,6 untuk Flash-1017 versus 56,3 untuk Opus. Harga pada layanan DeepSeek sendiri adalah $0,15 per juta token masukan dan $0,60 per juta token keluaran, dengan pembacaan cache pada $0,003/M. Titik akhir Pencarian dan Pengambilan baru dibatasi pada 5 QPS per akun; panggilan sisi server yang dirutekan melalui DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, atau Codex tetap gratis hingga 1 November 2026. Makalah pendamping berjudul "DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Mendorong Batas Kompresi Cache KV," menempatkan kisah memori di sampulnya, dan tiba di tengah-tengah rangkaian pekerjaan cache KV sisi inferensi yang terlacak selama sebulan terakhir. Konteksnya adalah 1 juta token dengan output maksimal pada atau di atas 256 ribu, dan pengambilan sampel yang disarankan adalah suhu 1.0, top_p 1.0. Ekonomi biaya sisi pengembang: merinci bagaimana aktivasi yang jarang dan panggilan pencarian sebesar $0,75/1K digabungkan untuk melemahkan saluran RAG pencarian yang dihosting yang bersaing pada volume token agen. Menandai risiko operasional: DeepSeek mengirimkan pembaruan sebagai perubahan konfigurasi diam-diam tanpa jendela penghentian formal, berbeda dengan siklus pengumuman OpenAI, Anthropic, dan Google. Mekanisme penagihan dan batas tarif: 5 RMB per 1K permintaan, batas 5 QPS, jendela gratis hingga 1 November. Catatan, daftar snapshot -1017 muncul sebentar lalu menghilang tanpa komentar resmi. Judul asli: DeepSeek Mengirimkan V4.1-Flash-1017 Dengan API Pencarian Web Langsung di Agen 552B MoE

Berita ini disusun dari laporan AI Weekly / The Decoder / MarkTechPost.

Xiaomi 18 Pro Varian Global Nongol di Database SDPPI Indonesia — Siap Rilis di Tanah Air

The global launch date of the Xiaomi 18 Pro series is yet to be announced, but the brand has already confirmed that the two smartphones will be offered with the same chipsets as their Chinese counterparts . Now, the global model number of the Xiaomi 18 Pro has been spotted on Indonesia’s SDPPI database, pointing to its possible launch in the country. About the SDPPI appearance, the smartphone carrying the model number ‘2609BPN61G’ has been listed under the Xiaomi branding, with PT Xiaomi Technology Indonesia mentioned as the applicant. Its certification is dated the 12th of October 2026, and the certificate number ‘127564/DJID/2026’ has been provided. While no key specifications or features have been revealed via the database, this appearance suggests that the Xiaomi 18 Pro is being prepared for the Indonesian market. However, its exact launch date and availability details are yet to be officially revealed. Regarding the chipsets, Xiaomi had previously confirmed through a teaser that the standard Pro model will be powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chip, whereas the Pro Max will be featuring the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. These are the same chipsets offered on the respective Chinese models. Speaking more, only the Xiaomi 18 Pro has been confirmed for the Indian market so far, and rumours have pointed to a possible December 2026 launch in the country . However, an official confirmation regarding this timeline is still awaited. The brand is also yet to announce when the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max will be unveiled globally. Following further updates, we’ll be able to confirm their launch timelines, pricing details, and more. Stay tuned until then. Redmi K100's green variant officially revealed before launch

The Redmi K100 is gearing up to join the brand’s latest flagship smartphone lineup in China. Starting today, Redmi has started teasing the standard model, highlighting its focus on battery life and gaming performance. The phone is expected to deliver several high-end features while keeping its price below the Pro models. Redmi has confirmed that the K100 standard edition will launch this month, with the company promising gaming performance comparable to the Pro models. The smartphone is already available for reservations through Xiaomi’s online store, JD.com, and Tmall in China. Its official tagline highlights a new baseline for flagship smartphones, with endurance and gaming capabilities at the forefront. The phone’s green variant was recently shown by Xiaomi Group president Lu Weibing. It features a design similar to the Redmi K100 Pro models but packs a dual-camera setup instead triple camera seen on the Pro variants. It is also confirmed to feature Bose-tuned speakers. According to leaks, the Redmi K100 could feature a 6.9-inch AMOLED display with 1.5K resolution and a 185Hz refresh rate. For performance, the phone is expected to use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset from 2024. A dedicated graphics chip could support simultaneous game super-resolution and frame interpolation for smoother gameplay. The Redmi K100 will house a 10,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, potentially making it the largest battery ever fitted to a Redmi K-series phone. A 100W wired charging system has also been confirmed through China’s 3C certification , although Xiaomi has yet to officially announce the battery capacity. Other reported features include an ultrasonic fingerprint scanner and an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance, though these details remain unconfirmed. Pricing has not been officially announced, but tipster Digital Chat Station previously suggested a starting price of around 3,500 yuan (approximately $490). The Redmi K100 is expected to sit below the K100 Pro and K100 Pro Max in the lineup. Review NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X rilis: GPU terkuat di laptop Windows, CPU-nya sudah 'ketinggalan'

Production review embargoes for NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X lifted this morning, and the first production review roundup from ComputerBase, HotHardware, Tom's Guide, Trusted Reviews, Windows Central, and KitGuru lands in two distinct halves: the GPU is genuinely the most capable integrated graphics package ever placed inside a Windows laptop, and the CPU uses ARM cores that MediaTek — the very company NVIDIA co-developed them with — has already surpassed in its own current smartphone lineup. Retail availability begins Thursday, October 16. For buyers ready to spend between $2,599 and roughly $6,700 on a first-wave RTX Spark laptop, the production benchmark data now answers the questions that months of prototype leaks and pre-launch software demos could not: the GPU performance and AI memory architecture are real; the CPU story carries a caveat that matters more the less your workflow is GPU-bound; and the memory bandwidth architecture imposes a ceiling on AI inference token speed that Apple's M4 Max still exceeds, for models small enough to fit on either platform. RTX Spark N1X is not a traditional laptop chip. It is a two-chiplet 2.5D package — a MediaTek-designed ARM CPU die and an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU die, manufactured separately on TSMC's 3nm process and integrated into a single unit connected by NVIDIA's NVLink C2C interconnect . The NVLink C2C delivers 600 GB/s of bidirectional bandwidth between the two dies, which is why NVIDIA's marketing materials quote that figure prominently. But 600 GB/s is the inter-die speed — how fast data moves between the CPU and GPU inside the package. The figure that governs AI inference performance and GPU memory throughput is the peak bandwidth to the shared physical LPDDR5X-9400 memory pool: 300 GB/s memory bandwidth over a 256-bit interface. Both chiplets draw from this pool. Up to 128 GB is available on flagship configurations, and up to 96 GB can be allocated to the GPU — more than any previous laptop GPU by a factor of four. The unified memory architecture is what makes RTX Spark categorically different from every previous Windows laptop. A 70-billion-parameter AI model quantized to 4 bits requires roughly 41 GB to load into memory. On any conventional laptop — regardless of how fast the discrete GPU is — that model cannot fit, because discrete GPUs ship with a maximum of 24 GB of VRAM, and the system DRAM and GPU VRAM are separate pools. On an RTX Spark laptop with 64 GB or more, that model loads and runs entirely on-device. Two hardware configurations go on sale beginning October 16:

Performance cores peak at 4.0–4.1 GHz on the large variant, 3.9 GHz on the smaller. The design traces its lineage to the GB10 "Grace Blackwell" Superchip inside NVIDIA's DGX Spark developer workstation, which launched in 2025 for $4,699. The N1X is the consumer-portable adaptation: ConnectX-7 networking interfaces removed, TDP capped at 80W in laptop form (versus 140W for the desktop version), and memory configurations starting at 24 GB. Read more: NVIDIA RTX Spark Launches Friday: 74-Billion-Parameter AI Fits in 24GB Laptop

The 6,144-shader configuration matches the CUDA core count of NVIDIA's desktop GeForce RTX 5070 and exceeds both the RTX 5070 Laptop GPU and the RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU in raw shader count. Dedicated GDDR7 memory in those discrete chips gives them higher bandwidth — up to 672 GB/s versus 300 GB/s on the N1X — but in 3DMark synthetic tests, the N1X's larger compute block and unified memory architecture produce clear advantages. In 3DMark Time Spy Extreme, the N1X scored 6,060 — against 4,689 for AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo) and 3,226 for Intel's top mobile chip. Steel Nomad: 2,912 (N1X) versus 1,895 (AMD) and 1,483 (Intel). Solar Bay ray tracing: 10,594 (N1X) against 6,047 (AMD) and 4,015 (Intel). In real-game testing, Trusted Reviews reported Cyberpunk 2077 at 1080p Ultra settings averaging nearly 70 frames per second — playable, and genuinely impressive for a 60–80W TDP envelope. Frame rates fell to around 47 fps at QHD. Heavy ray tracing at Ultra presets pushed closer to 30 fps at 1080p — the bandwidth constraint becoming visible. ComputerBase found the platform delivers more than double the efficiency of a discrete GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU paired with an x86 CPU at roughly 60W TDP, because the discrete GPU alone typically requires at least 50W, leaving almost no power budget for the CPU. That efficiency advantage translates to the battery performance HotHardware's Marco Chiappetta measured on the Surface Laptop Ultra review : 14 hours and 35 minutes of video playback, with the system producing full performance on battery and not just while plugged in. NVIDIA claimed this at Computex; the production data confirms it. Chiappetta's verdict: "In its most potent form, the RTX Spark N1X is a powerful SoC that offers competitive multi-threaded CPU performance versus today's top mobile platforms, with class-leading GPU performance."

The Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 cores inside the N1X are ARM's 2024-generation designs. ComputerBase noted — pointedly — that MediaTek, NVIDIA's CPU partner on this chip, has already shipped ARM's newer C2 architecture in its own Dimensity 9600 Pro. Engineering samples of the N1X reportedly date back to 2024, suggesting a development timeline that slipped significantly from original targets. That age shows in single-threaded benchmarks. In Geekbench 7, the 20-core N1X scored approximately 2,604–2,710 single-core — competitive with Snapdragon X Elite territory but trailing Apple's M5 Pro. In Cinebench 2026 single-core, scores cluster around 555–558 across reviewers' units, landing roughly between Apple's M3 and M4. Multi-core tells a more favorable story. HotHardware found multi-core CPU throughput competitive with the Apple M4 Pro and Intel's Core Ultra 9 285K desktop chip. Windows Central benchmarked Geekbench 7 multi-core at 23,571; Tom's Guide reported 26,310 on the same test. The spread reflects different test systems and configurations across the first-wave OEM lineup. PassMark's publicly submitted PerformanceTest CPU database gives the 20-core N1X a CPU Mark of approximately 42,224 in multi-threaded workloads and a single-thread rating of 4,452 — placing it 350th overall and 98th in single-thread performance among the 6,050 processors tracked in the database. The practical summary: for workloads that scale across many threads — code compilation, video encoding, multi-threaded scientific computing — the CPU is genuinely competitive with today's best mobile platforms. For single-threaded tasks like gaming engine logic, web browser performance, and interactive applications, it trails Apple's current M5 generation by a meaningful margin. RTX Spark's AI case rests on two distinct advantages: memory capacity and software ecosystem. On capacity, 128 GB unified memory enables loading and running models that no previous laptop could handle at all. At 4-bit quantization, a 70-billion-parameter model requires roughly 41 GB — comfortably within the 64 GB and 128 GB configurations. NVIDIA claims support for models up to 120 billion parameters with context lengths up to one million tokens. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B — available for download today — uses sparse mixture-of-experts architecture to activate only 9 billion of its 74 billion parameters per inference, fitting into 24 GB while retaining frontier-class reasoning capability. On software ecosystem, CUDA is confirmed working on production RTX Spark units — the pre-production CUDA failures documented in July 2026 on prototype hardware were driver-related and have been resolved. TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM, PyTorch's CUDA backend, llama.cpp-for-CUDA, and the broader NVIDIA AI platform now run natively on the N1X. This ecosystem is RTX Spark's deepest structural advantage over AMD Ryzen AI Max hardware, which relies on ROCm — a GPU compute platform that supports the major frameworks but lacks CUDA's fifteen-year depth of community tooling. The caveat buyers need: LPDDR5X memory at 300 GB/s is the binding constraint for token-generation speed. AI inference in large language models is memory-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound — the GPU's processing units must continuously stream model weight data from DRAM during token generation, and the rate of that stream sets the tokens-per-second ceiling. Apple's M4 Max delivers approximately 540 GB/s bandwidth from its monolithic SoC design, nearly double RTX Spark's figure. For models that fit within both platforms' memory — which includes everything up to roughly 70B parameters at 4-bit quantization — Apple's platform generates tokens faster. RTX Spark wins on capacity (models too large for Apple's current configs fit here) and on CUDA ecosystem depth. Apple wins on tokens-per-second for models below the ~96 GB ceiling. Buyers choosing between them for AI inference work need to know which constraint matters more to their specific workflow. The 55 TOPS neural processing unit included in the N1X is, for now, reserved exclusively for Microsoft Copilot+ features and is inaccessible to third-party software — a significant constraint NVIDIA confirmed to ComputerBase. NVIDIA confirmed today, alongside the review embargo lift, the arrival of an updated DLSS 5 model deploying first in NBA 2K27 Season 2 on October 16. The updated model reduces its parameter count to approximately 118 million — roughly 24% smaller than its predecessor — and cuts 4K VRAM usage by 20%, according to NVIDIA. HotHardware separately reported figures of up to 35% faster on an RTX 5060 compared to the previous DLSS 5 version, with the improvement coming from a lighter algorithm for the optical flow model that Frame Generation relies on. For RTX Spark specifically, this matters beyond the headline frame-rate number: Multi Frame Generation at up to 6x generates multiple display frames from a single rendered frame, directly reducing the effective bandwidth demand per displayed output. That is the software-layer mitigation for the hardware 300 GB/s bandwidth ceiling. NVIDIA characterized the new model as roughly ten times more efficient than the original March demonstration that required dual RTX 5090 GPUs, and twice as fast as the September version. The update applies simultaneously to GeForce RTX 50-series GPUs, GeForce NOW, and RTX Spark laptops. Hogwarts Legacy will receive DLSS 5 on November 5; RTX Remix will gain DLSS 5 support for modders on October 23. All first-wave RTX Spark laptops ship with Windows 11 on Arm. ComputerBase's compatibility assessment described the experience as "not a catastrophe" — language that accurately captures both the genuine progress made since Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite restarted the Windows-on-Arm platform in 2024 and the gaps that remain. NVIDIA confirmed day-one native ARM anti-cheat support for Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, Rocket League, The Finals, and several other titles. Games with kernel-level anti-cheat that have not yet shipped native ARM builds remain incompatible through the Prism emulation layer. The most notable gap for a large portion of the gaming audience: Call of Duty arrives in 2027 for RTX Spark. Microsoft is deepening Windows integration around the platform for launch: general availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) for agent sandboxing, expanded Copilot local-model support, and a new Get Started experience that auto-configures popular AI agent platforms on first boot. Read more: Surface Laptop Ultra Prototype Leak Reveals RTX Spark CUDA Failures Before Fall Launch

Peak system power consumption on the Surface Laptop Ultra reached 138W transiently during intensive workloads, suggesting the N1X boosts beyond its official 80W envelope when thermal and power headroom permits. The 80W TDP is a sustained rating, not a ceiling, and first-wave OEMs have clearly designed their thermal systems with burst capacity in mind. On battery, a Speedometer browser benchmark showed an 18% performance reduction versus plugged-in on the Surface Laptop Ultra — better than most competing systems at similar price points, and consistent with NVIDIA's Computex claim that RTX Spark machines deliver full performance regardless of power source. That claim holds for the GPU under real-world workloads; the 18% CPU headroom reduction on battery is the qualifier. First-wave RTX Spark laptops go on sale October 16 from HP, ASUS, MSI, Dell, Lenovo (Yoga 9n 2-in-1), and Microsoft (Surface Laptop Ultra). ComputerBase's review tested the ASUS ProArt P16 (H7607) configured with the 20-core N1X, 64 GB of memory, and a 1 TB SSD at €4,299 (approximately $4,819 USD). A smaller ASUS ProArt P14 with 32 GB starts at €3,299 (approximately $3,698 USD). The US entry point across the lineup — a 24 GB N1X configuration — begins at $2,599 , according to HotHardware. Mini-PC form factors from Acer and others are expected to follow, using the higher-TDP 140W configuration of the same N1X chip at desktop power limits. NVIDIA's published roadmap indicates that lower-power N1 variants — with 10- or 12-core CPUs and 2,048–2,560 GPU shaders — are in development for more affordable configurations below the $2,599 floor. The successor platform — RTX Spark with Vera and Rubin successor architecture — is currently targeted for 2028. For AI developers, data scientists, and researchers who need to run models in the 30B–120B parameter range locally on a portable Windows device, RTX Spark N1X is the only option that exists at any price. No other laptop delivers more than 24 GB of usable GPU memory. The CUDA ecosystem is now confirmed working on production hardware, and the entry price of $2,599 is substantially below what comparable model-capacity workstations have historically cost. For content creators working in NVIDIA-optimized applications — Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Blender, ComfyUI — the combination of confirmed CUDA stack, GPU efficiency advantage, and up to 128 GB for large project assets makes RTX Spark a credible professional platform. The CPU age caveat matters less when the GPU bottleneck dominates the workflow. For mainstream gaming buyers, the picture is less straightforward. The GPU delivers playable performance in modern titles within its thermal envelope, and DLSS 5's updated model substantially extends frame-rate reach for supported games. But Call of Duty's absence until 2027, the WoA anti-cheat patchwork for other titles, and a starting price of $2,599 make this a harder sell than the GPU benchmark numbers alone suggest. For buyers comparing directly to Apple's MacBook Pro M4 Pro or M4 Max: RTX Spark wins on GPU compute, CUDA ecosystem depth, and memory capacity ceiling; Apple's M-series wins on single-core CPU performance, tokens-per-second AI inference speed for models below 96 GB, and a more mature software ecosystem for the mainstream Mac application library. The right choice depends on which constraint matters more to the work you actually do. (Exchange rate as of October 15, 2026; conversions are approximate.)

In multi-threaded workloads — video encoding, code compilation, scientific computing — production benchmarks place the 20-core N1X close to Apple's M4 Pro. In single-threaded performance, which governs gaming engine responsiveness, browser speed, and interactive application latency, the RTX Spark trails Apple's M5 generation by a meaningful margin. ComputerBase's finding is the key context: the Cortex-X925 cores inside the N1X are already two generations behind MediaTek's own current smartphone lineup, which has moved to ARM's newer C2 architecture. Yes on capacity: 70-billion-parameter models at 4-bit quantization require roughly 41 GB, well within a 64 GB or 128 GB RTX Spark configuration. But "faster" depends on which constraint matters. Apple's M4 Max delivers approximately 540 GB/s bandwidth versus RTX Spark's 300 GB/s, meaning it generates tokens faster per second for any model that fits within Apple's memory ceiling. RTX Spark's advantage is (a) models too large for Apple's base configurations — anything requiring more than 48–96 GB — and (b) CUDA-specific software workflows (TensorRT, PyTorch CUDA backend, llama.cpp-for-CUDA) that Apple Silicon does not support. Call of Duty will not be available on RTX Spark until 2027. Other games with kernel-level anti-cheat that have not yet shipped native ARM builds remain incompatible through Windows on Arm's Prism emulation layer. Day-one native ARM support is confirmed for Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, Rocket League, The Finals, and other titles whose publishers have integrated ARM-native anti-cheat support . The updated DLSS 5 model reduces its parameter count by approximately 24% and cuts 4K VRAM usage by 20%. For RTX Spark, the significance extends beyond raw frame-rate improvement: Multi Frame Generation at up to 6x generates multiple display frames from a single rendered frame, reducing effective per-frame bandwidth demand. Since RTX Spark's GPU is constrained to 300 GB/s of LPDDR5X bandwidth — compared to 672 GB/s for discrete GDDR7 laptop GPUs — DLSS 5 acts as a software-layer mitigation for a hardware architectural ceiling. iQOO Neo12 dikonfirmasi: layar 2K 185Hz, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, baterai 9.000mAh

The iQOO Neo series hasn’t seen a new launch in India since the Neo 10 arrived in 2025, making an upgrade overdue for buyers looking for a performance-focused phone in the segment. However, confirmed details of the upcoming iQOO Neo12 have now emerged in China, with the company confirming a new high-refresh-rate display, a flagship Snapdragon chipset, and a larger battery ahead of its launch later this month. iQOO has confirmed that the iQOO Neo12 will feature a 2K OLED display supplied by Chinese manufacturer Visionox, with a 185Hz refresh rate. The company has also shared teaser images offering an early look at the phone’s display and rear design. The display teaser shows a flat panel with slim, uniform bezels and a punch-hole selfie camera, and highlights the collaboration between Visionox, iQOO, and Tsinghua University on display technology. iQOO will reveal more details at an event on October 14th. Visionox’s panel uses p-TSF luminescent technology, designed to improve colour reproduction, reduce power consumption, and extend display lifespan. Tipster Digital Chat Station has previously said the Neo12 will be the first smartphone to use Visionox’s fourth-generation p-TSF material, which hasn’t appeared on any flagship phones that have been launching since September this year. The other teaser uses a red-and-black design, with the phone partially concealed beneath textured red fabric. It reveals part of a black rear camera module with a large circular camera element and a vent-like element. The teaser has the text “Monster Inside” indicating heavy performance. Under the hood, the Neo12 will feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset, iQOO’s in-house Q3 gaming chip, and a new Ice-Dome cooling system with an active fan. It will also pack a 9,000mAh battery, up from the 7,500mAh unit in the iQOO Neo11. For context, the Neo11 features a 6.82-inch 2K LTPO AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate, the Snapdragon 8 Elite processor, and a Q2 gaming chip paired with a dedicated liquid-cooling system. The Neo12’s confirmed specifications suggest improvements in refresh rate, processing power, cooling hardware, and battery capacity. Camera specifications, charging speeds, memory options, and durability ratings are yet to be announced. The 185Hz refresh rate is a huge upgrade for sure, but we don’t know whether it will be available system-wide or limited to supported games. iQOO has confirmed the display specification, but the announcements do not clarify how the refresh rate will work across apps and games. OnePlus debuted the OnePlus 16 with a system-wide 165Hz refresh rate going up to 185Hz for specific titles, so the iQOO Neo12 might compete with that. iQOO hasn’t confirmed the Neo12’s exact launch date, but the phone is already available for pre-order in China. More details are expected in the coming weeks. According to a report, the smartphone could reach select global markets as the iQOO 16R with the same specifications. A Geekbench listing reportedly associated with the device suggests 16GB of RAM, Android 17-based OriginOS 7, and an Adreno 840 GPU. These details remain unconfirmed by iQOO. India availability is also less certain though a tipster recently said the phone will arrive in the country. The iQOO Neo11 did not launch here, leaving the Neo10, which debuted in 2025, as the latest model in the Indian Neo lineup. The phone starts below Rs 45,000 and has since received new colour options and price increases. With the Neo10 now more than a year old, the Neo12 could be a deserved upgrade if iQOO brings it to India. Its combination of a flagship chipset, active cooling, a 185Hz display, and a 9,000mAh battery could appeal to mobile gamers. However, buyers should wait for confirmation of an Indian launch.
